svg.text: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867. As a girl she loved science, but at that time
women were not allowed to study at university in Poland, so in 1891 she moved to
Paris, where she studied physics and mathematics.
In Paris she met Pierre Curie, a scientist, and they married in 1895. Together they
studied radioactivity, and in 1898 they discovered two new elements: polonium, which
Marie named after her homeland, and radium. In 1903, she, her husband and another
scientist shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.
After Pierre died in an accident in 1906, Marie continued working alone and became the
first woman to teach at the University of Paris. In 1911, she won a second Nobel
Prize, this time in Chemistry. During the First World War she organised mobile X-ray
units to help wounded soldiers. She died in 1934, and today she is remembered as one
of the greatest scientists in history.
